approval_required_for: Any architecture change, pipeline-topology change, memory-layout change, numeric-policy or tolerance change, or major trusted-template change proposed during repair.
Any replacement or modification of the exact sample-project wrapper/source identity; such a change requires a new verification contract and restart rather than an in-loop hash update.

Any ambiguous board/app-shell top, wrapper, fileset, clock, XDC, synthesis target, bitstream target, or runtime target that cannot be resolved uniquely from supplied source identities and real tool evidence.
Any proposed lower-layer backtrack not already justified by a contradictory current-layer boundary trace.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not publish the refined selector or permit Stage 7 consumption. Record the unbound node, missing producer/checker, cycle, identity gap, or cut violation in the refinement audit and issue a bounded Stage 6 retry request.
executable_actions.rationale: Materialize the accepted final refinement from all four specialist artifacts, preserve the 36-node producer/checker coverage, encode current-certificate invalidity, and keep backend work beyond the board-semantic cut.

executable_actions.on_failure: Classify missing tensor coverage, target-model execution, explicit tolerance, same-input identity, semantic harness, or DUT binding as a verification/golden-reference capability blocker. Do not use sampled weights, random expected values, RTL-derived expected values, a default model, or a legacy fallback test.
executable_actions.rationale: Create the immutable checkpoint, input, independent target-model, numeric, semantic-testbench, and DUT weight-binding evidence required before any current-contract functional pass. Catalog the complete checkpoint while marking only Transformer-block tensors as DUT-required.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep single-layer and all higher scopes blocked and invoke stage7.repair_failed_operator_leaf. Do not promote partial leaf coverage or alter the immutable comparison contract.
executable_actions.rationale: Supersede the stale operator-leaf certificate by verifying every generated Transformer-block leaf against the immutable target-model boundary evidence and executed real-weight bindings.

executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at operator-leaf closure. If localization is inconclusive, request additional instrumentation; if the required change affects architecture, pipeline topology, memory layout, numeric policy, tolerance, or a major template boundary, issue an approval/backtrack request instead of free-form RTL modification.
executable_actions.rationale: Enforce tool-output to earliest-boundary localization to bounded template repair to targeted rerun at the operator-leaf layer.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep board AXI/DDR closure and backend blocked and invoke stage7.repair_failed_single_layer. Do not reopen a certified leaf unless the single-layer trace identifies a contradictory leaf boundary.
executable_actions.rationale: Supersede the stale single-layer certificate by connecting only currently certified leaves and verifying layer-level values, stream order, casts, and complete bound-weight use under the same immutable contract.

executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at single-layer closure. Generate a targeted lower-layer backtrack only when the bound trace contradicts the leaf certificate; otherwise request additional current-layer instrumentation or approval for any major contract change.
executable_actions.rationale: Localize the earliest connected-layer contract violation and repair only bounded template, connection, buffering, or instrumentation logic before rerunning the failed single-layer checker.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not start Vivado. If discovery is ambiguous, invoke stage7.resolve_ambiguous_board_target; otherwise invoke stage7.repair_failed_board_layer using the functional_sim trace and earliest violated boundary.
executable_actions.rationale: Execute the third repair-loop layer using the exact user sample-project wrapper and simulation sources. functional_sim is the sole canonical source for multi-layer, deadlock, AXI, DDR, numeric, and board-semantic classifiers.

executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at board AXI/DDR closure and preserve checkpoint, stimulus, reference, numeric policy, tolerance, testbench, and exact-wrapper hashes. Backtrack to the single-layer or leaf scope only if the board trace contradicts the corresponding certified boundary; request approval for architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric, or wrapper-contract changes.
executable_actions.rationale: Localize real liveness, value, order, address, transfer, loader, or protocol failure in the exact wrapped system and repair only the violating DUT, loader/harness, instrumentation, or bounded integration logic.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep board functional simulation, Vivado, bitstream, and board runtime blocked until one target is supported by cited source/tool evidence and explicit approval.
executable_actions.rationale: Real sample-project evidence may expose multiple plausible wrapper, fileset, clock, XDC, or app-shell targets. The agent must synthesize evidence-cited candidates and obtain approval rather than guess names.

executable_actions.on_failure: Retain the downstream blocklist for case_vivado_synthesis, case_vivado_implementation, case_runtime_bitstream, case_runtime_abi_check, and board_runtime; do not reinterpret configured or smoke evidence as board functional closure.
executable_actions.rationale: Enforce the strict cut: only a current-contract-valid board semantic aggregate may release downstream Vivado and runtime planning, while board runtime remains necessary for final design closure.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not claim final hardware pass. Feed real reports or runtime logs to downstream.classify_backend_failure; retain valid lower-layer certificates unless the backend evidence contains a bound contradiction to their functional traces.
executable_actions.rationale: Execute implementation and physical runtime only after the verification-to-backend release. These nodes are downstream obligations and do not contribute retroactively to Stage 7 board-functional acceptance.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the failed backend/runtime node and all dependent nodes blocked. Escalate ambiguous target selection through the approval-bound discovery action and do not modify golden evidence, tolerance, or exact wrapper identity.
executable_actions.rationale: Turn real Vivado, bitstream, ABI, or runtime failure evidence into a bounded recovery, approval request, or checker-grounded backtrack rather than relying on static scripts or operator memory.

observations: The supplied verification_plan_static_check, hierarchical_verification_plan_check, verification_artifact_contract_check, tool_protocol_check, sacg_reference_check, required_real_tool_evidence_check, and repair-boundary evidence pass for the current Stage 6 contract. These are static/configuration passes, not real-tool functional passes.

The compact role slice omits detailed required_evidence_gates, evidence_path_requirements, and most protocol rows, but presence_summary reports 27 evidence gates, 36 evidence-path requirements, 34 required tool protocols, and 36 DAG nodes. Under role_slice_policy, the empty visible arrays are not treated as missing fields because verification_artifact_contract_check passed.

Producer/checker coverage is complete: semantic roots bind to case_real_weight_artifacts, case_target_model_reference, and case_semantic_testbench; all nine leaf records bind to case_stage_leaf_static; leaf simulation, comparison, and aggregation bind to case_leaf_functional, case_leaf_golden_compare, and case_operator_leaf_semantic_evidence; layer-two nodes bind to case_tb_scaffold, case_single_transformer_layer/single_transformer_layer, case_single_layer_functional, case_single_layer_golden_compare, and case_single_layer_semantic_evidence.

Third-layer producer/checker coverage is complete: case_multilayer_pipeline, case_board_interface_discovery, and case_axi_ddr_interface prepare the exact wrapped system; case_vcs_functional_sim produces canonical real simulator evidence; case_multilayer_functional, case_pipeline_deadlock_check, case_axi_protocol_check, and case_ddr_image_roundtrip classify only that functional_sim evidence; case_board_semantic_evidence is the mandatory aggregate.

Downstream producer/checker coverage is configured for case_vivado_synthesis, case_vivado_implementation, case_runtime_bitstream, case_runtime_abi_check, and board_runtime, but those nodes are outside current Stage 7 board-functional closure and cannot satisfy or replace case_board_semantic_evidence.

The topological order is acyclic and preserves the three-layer repair discipline: operator leaves, then connected single transformer layer, then the exact board AXI/DDR wrapped multi-layer system. A higher-layer failure may reopen a lower layer only through a contradictory bound boundary trace and targeted backtrack.

Current certificate validation is decisive: artifact.stage7.operator_leaf_promotion_certificate and artifact.stage7.single_layer_promotion_certificate exist but have current_contract_valid=false and reuse_allowed=false; artifact.stage7.board_axi_ddr_promotion_certificate is absent. Historical Stage 7 pass summaries therefore cannot select a higher scope.

The refined selector starts at operator_leaf_closure, advances to single_layer_closure only after a new current-contract-valid leaf certificate, and advances to board_axi_ddr_closure only after a new current-contract-valid single-layer certificate. Backend release requires a new board semantic certificate.

Immutable identity propagation must include the complete target-checkpoint tensor catalog and hashes, Transformer-block DUT-scope classification, deterministic or real stimulus provenance and hash, independent target-model boundary-output hashes, numeric policy and tolerance hash, semantic testbench hashes, generated RTL/package hashes, bound loader/harness hashes, executed per-tensor DUT-consumption evidence, and exact sample-project wrapper/source hashes.

The target-model reference must execute the real target model on the same checkpoint and stimulus used by the DUT. Random generation is permitted only for input stimulus; expected values may not be random, RTL-derived, identity/default outputs, or modified during repair.

DUT correctness and weight-consumption scope is exactly the Transformer blocks. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail functions remain excluded from DUT golden boundaries and DUT weight-coverage requirements, while the checkpoint catalog still records their out-of-scope classification.

Stage 3 model/shape/dataflow evidence, Stage 4 numeric and parameter bindings, and Stage 5 compile/elaboration/package evidence are ready. Dynamic value, order, liveness, AXI, DDR, and board-wrapper behavior remains pending real Stage 7 execution.

The exact wrapper and simulation sources must be discovered from artifact.input.sample_project_index and hashed before third-layer execution. No simplified wrapper, guessed module name, or hardcoded project path may substitute for the supplied project.

Parameter records contain clock_target_mhz=0. Because parameter static checks passed, this is not a current Stage 6 blocker; downstream synthesis must obtain clock and XDC facts from the exact sample project or request bounded approval rather than guessing a target frequency.
SACG memory truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. Historical outcomes are retained as recovery evidence but create no current Stage 6 blocker.
No functional hardware pass, Vivado pass, bitstream pass, runtime ABI pass, or physical-board pass is claimed by this refinement.
proposed_actions: Publish the five refined Stage 6 artifacts only with the audited producer/checker bindings and strict backend cut encoded.
Generate a fresh immutable semantic baseline from the selected checkpoint and stimulus before rerunning any functional layer.
Re-execute operator-leaf closure under real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2 and issue a certificate only after all nine leaves, golden comparisons, weight-consumption checks, and identity checks pass.
Re-execute connected single-layer closure only after the fresh leaf certificate validates under the current contract.
Discover and hash the exact sample-project wrapper, then execute the board-accurate functional simulator and derive every third-layer classifier from that single run.
On any layer failure, run failure slicing, CCTG/boundary-guided earliest-cause localization, bounded template repair, and targeted rerun at the same layer; do not skip upward.
Release backend planning only after case_board_semantic_evidence and the board AXI/DDR promotion certificate pass; leave Vivado, bitstream, ABI, and board runtime downstream.
If board/app-shell target discovery is ambiguous, issue a bounded approval request rather than selecting names or paths heuristically.
risks: Reusing either historical lower-layer certificate without current-contract validation would permit stale checkpoint, stimulus, tolerance, harness, RTL, or weight-binding identities to contaminate higher-layer evidence.
A manifest on disk is insufficient weight evidence. Promotion would be unsound if executed loader/harness traces do not prove consumption of every required Transformer-block tensor bound to the DUT.

Any expected-output path derived from random data, RTL output, a default/identity implementation, logits outside accelerator scope, or a different checkpoint/stimulus would invalidate semantic comparison.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model outputs, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench contract, or exact board-wrapper source hashes during a repair loop would make before/after evidence incomparable.

If third-layer classifiers consume separate smoke runs rather than the canonical functional_sim evidence identity, liveness, value, ordering, AXI, and DDR conclusions could refer to different executions.

A value mismatch can originate in numeric casts, stream/lane order, transfer count, address mapping, loader binding, or wrapper integration. Repairing a downstream symptom before locating the earliest violated boundary risks masking the cause.
Beginning Vivado synthesis or implementation before case_board_semantic_evidence passes would violate the functional-before-backend cut and could waste backend work on a semantically invalid system.
An ambiguous sample-project top, wrapper, fileset, clock, XDC, or runtime target must not be guessed. It requires evidence-backed bounded recovery and explicit approval.
Downstream backend failure does not automatically invalidate lower-layer functional certificates; reopening them without a contradictory boundary trace would violate the anti-spin policy.
